약하다 = WEAK; 강하다 = strong. Picture a flimsy paper bridge versus a strong steel bridge. Not the medicine noun 약.

note: The new page also says sensitive. 약하다 means weak; sensitive is usually 예민하다 / 민감하다 (skin: 민감하다).

memoryHint.text: 개인 = individual/person; 정보 = information. PERSONAL INFORMATION. Picture a private name/address card with a little lock.

note: Paper: личная info. 개인정보 means personal information/data (also written without a space).

memoryHint.text: Picture lifting a photo UP to a website: UPLOAD/POST. The same upward motion helps with raise/lift in other contexts.

note: Paper: to post. Online it means post/upload; in other contexts it can mean raise or lift.

memoryHint.text: 쓸모 = usefulness; 없다 = doesn't exist. NO USEFULNESS → useless. Picture a broken umbrella full of holes.
ma-eul → a MILE of little houses: a VILLAGE. Picture a small community, not the whole countryside.
시골 = COUNTRYSIDE; 마을 = a village within it. Picture a tiny village surrounded by huge green rural fields.

note: Paper: деревня, провинция. 시골 is the countryside/rural area; a particular village is 마을.

memoryHint.text: byeok → 'BAM!' into a brick WALL. Imagine bumping gently into a wall and pointing at it: 벽.
Draw a coloured REGION on a map. 지역 = area/region; it is the area itself, not the road through it.
Picture a fact-checker stamping 'TRUE': 사실 = FACT/TRUTH. 사실… can also introduce 'actually…'.
소개 (noun) = introduction; 소개하다 (verb) = introduce; 소개되다 (passive verb) = be introduced. The 하다 form turns the noun into an action/state.

quizAnswer: 소개 = introduction; 소개하다 = introduce; 소개되다 = be introduced
note: One family card: grammatical forms are labelled in the checked meaning.

familyHints.text: 소개 = INTRODUCTION; 자기소개 = self-introduction; 소개하다 = introduce. Picture an introduction card passed between two strangers.
소개 = introduction; 하다 = do. INTRODUCE someone. Picture a host presenting you with a microphone.
소개하다 = introduce; 되다 makes it passive. 소개되다 = BE INTRODUCED. Picture someone else introducing you.

memoryHint.text: 상영 = screening a film; 관 = 館, hall. FILM-SCREENING HALL → cinema auditorium. It is the room, not the screen itself.

note: Your paper says “movie theatre screen”; 상영관 is the room where a film is shown.

memoryHint.text: Picture a sports PLAYER in a numbered jersey, standing on the pitch. 선수 = athlete/player.
한 개 = one item; 밖에 + 없다 = nothing except. NOTHING EXCEPT ONE → only one. Picture one lonely coin.

quizAnswer: have only one / there is only one
note: Paper: only. 한 개 = one item; 밖에 + negative expresses only. Literally there isn't anything except one.

memoryHint.text: 걷다 becomes 걸- before this ending; -(으)면 = if. IF YOU WALK. Picture an IF sign over a walking path.

note: Your paper says “if you want”, but the handwriting reads 걸으면 = if you walk. If you want = 원하면. Check the photo.

memoryHint.text: yu-reop is the Korean form of EUROPE. Picture the European continent shaped like the syllables 유럽.
그립다 = miss/long for; 그리운 describes someone/something missed. Picture the same treasured photo as 그립습니다.

note: An adjective form of 그립다 (to miss / long for); your paper says “to miss”.

memoryHint.text: 생각 = thought; 나다 = arise. A THOUGHT ARISES → remember/come to mind. Picture a memory suddenly popping up.

note: Your paper says “think”. 생각나다 means come to mind / remember; think = 생각하다.

memoryHint.text: 이용 = use; 시간 = time. USE TIME → hours when a facility is available. Picture opening hours on a door.

note: Paper: usage time. On a facility notice it often means the hours when you may use the facility.

memoryHint.text: 부 = 不, not; 족 = 足, enough here. NOT ENOUGH → lacking. Picture a puzzle missing its final piece.
동 = 動, move. Picture being ACTIVE and moving from one activity to another; same 동 in 동물.
도전 (noun) = challenge / attempt; 도전하다 (verb) = take on a challenge. The 하다 form turns the noun into an action/state.

quizAnswer: 도전 = challenge / attempt; 도전하다 = take on a challenge
note: One family card: grammatical forms are labelled in the checked meaning. Paper: try (challenge). 도전 is a noun; 도전하다 = take on a challenge / attempt.

familyHints.text: Picture accepting a CHALLENGE by stepping toward a tall climbing wall. 도전하다 = take on the challenge.

memoryHint.text: Picture a progress graph going UP: your condition GETS BETTER. Link it to your Korean improving each day.
물 = water; 병 = bottle. WATER BOTTLE. Compare 꽃병 = flower bottle → vase.
Picture a GUARD keeping a promise and protecting a gate. 지키다 = keep/protect/guard, according to context.

note: Your paper says “protect / safe”. 지키다 is a verb: protect / keep / guard.

memoryHint.text: 여러 = several; 가지 = kinds; -로 = by/in. IN SEVERAL KINDS OF WAYS → in various ways.
po-gi → 'FORGET IT!' Someone gives up and puts the unfinished game away. GIVE UP, not simply pause.
Picture an arrow pointing the OPPOSITE way and a person objecting: 반대 can be the opposite or opposition.

note: Paper: disagreement. 반대 can mean opposing something or the opposite; 반대하다 = oppose/object.

memoryHint.text: Turn a severity dial all the way up: SEVERE/INTENSE. 감기가 심해요 = the cold is bad/severe.

note: Paper: too extreme. 심하다 describes severity/intensity: 감기가 심하다 = have a bad cold.

memoryHint.text: Picture answering the phone: 'Is Anastasiia there?' '네, 전데요'—YES, SPEAKING / it's me.

note: A polite phrase often used when answering a phone call and confirming you are the person being asked for.

memoryHint.text: 소 = 所, place. Your dwelling PLACE written on an envelope → ADDRESS. Compare 매표소, ticket place.
Picture FIXING a broken chair—or correcting a mistake with an eraser. 고치다 covers fixing/correcting.
Picture a passport filled with stamps from things you've EXPERIENCED. 경험 is experience; 체험하다 = experience firsthand.
긴장 (noun) = tension / nervousness; 긴장하다 (verb) = be nervous / tense. The 하다 form turns the noun into an action/state.

quizAnswer: 긴장 = tension / nervousness; 긴장하다 = be nervous / tense
note: One family card: grammatical forms are labelled in the checked meaning. Paper: nervous / напряжение. This is a verb. 긴장 is the noun tension; 긴장하다 = become tense or nervous.

familyHints.text: 긴장 = TENSION/nervousness; 긴장하다 = feel tense. Picture a tight rubber band across your nervous shoulders.
긴장 = tension; 하다 = do/become. Your shoulders TENSE UP → be nervous. Picture relaxing them to release 긴장.

memoryHint.text: Spread all TEN fingers: 열. Use native Korean numbers for age/counters, e.g. 열 살, ten years old.

note: Used for counting and age. 열 개 = ten items; 열 살 = ten years old.

memoryHint.text: 스물 = TWENTY, but 스무 before a counter. Picture 20 candles: 스무 살. The ㄹ falls off before the counter.

note: Before a counter, 스물 becomes 스무: 스무 개 / 스무 살.

memoryHint.text: seo-reun → THIRTY friends having a party. Place 서른 on the third ten-step of your number ladder: 10, 20, 30.

note: Used for counting and age: 서른 개 / 서른 살.

memoryHint.text: ma-heun → 'MA has FORTY balloons'. Picture Mum surrounded by exactly four bunches of ten balloons.

note: Used for counting and age: 마흔 개 / 마흔 살.

memoryHint.text: swin → SWIM for FIFTY lengths. Picture a swimming scoreboard showing 50 next to 쉰.

note: Used for counting and age: 쉰 개 / 쉰 살.

memoryHint.text: 인 = 人, person. Imagine two PEOPLE greeting each other and bowing: 인사하다 = greet/say hello.
Picture DECIDING on a date and SETTING it in ink. 정하다 = decide/set; not chaos, even if a messy planner helps you remember.

note: Paper: chaos. The handwritten Korean reads 정하다, meaning decide / determine / set. Chaos is 혼란. Check the photo if you intended another word.

memoryHint.text: a-i → 'AYE!' shouts a little CHILD playing pirate. Picture a child, not an adult, with a toy pirate hat.
오른 = right; 손 = hand. RIGHT HAND. Point to it; compare 왼손, left hand.
Picture an oval EGG hanging like a tiny moon over your breakfast. 달걀 = egg; the moon picture is only an association.
Picture a PASSPORT opening like a book of travel permissions. Put 여권 beside 해외여행 and 공항 for one travel story.
해 = year here; 올해 = THIS YEAR. Circle the current year on your calendar. Compare 작년, last year, and 내년, next year.
Picture a POSTCARD with one big holiday PHOTO on the front. A letter (편지) is usually inside an envelope.

note: Your paper groups 엽서 / 편지 as letter. 엽서 = postcard; 편지 = letter.

memoryHint.text: 편지 = LETTER. Imagine a personal message tucked in an envelope; 엽서 = postcard with the picture on display.
등록 (noun) = registration; 등록하다 (verb) = register / enrol. The 하다 form turns the noun into an action/state.

note: One family card: grammatical forms are labelled in the checked meaning.

familyHints.text: 등록 = registration; 하다 = do. Picture writing your name into a registration list. 신청 = APPLY; 등록 = REGISTER/enrol.

memoryHint.text: 전시 (noun) = display / exhibition; 전시하다 (verb) = display / exhibit. The 하다 form turns the noun into an action/state.

quizAnswer: 전시 = display / exhibition; 전시하다 = display / exhibit
note: One family card: grammatical forms are labelled in the checked meaning.

familyHints.text: 전시 = display; 하다 = do. DISPLAY the paintings; 전시회 is the exhibition event where people see them.

memoryHint.text: Highlight only the latest few squares on a timeline: RECENTLY/LATELY. Compare 예전에, long ago, at its far end.

note: Your paper says recent. 최근 refers to the recent past; 최근에 = recently.

memoryHint.text: Picture a suitcase LEAVING the station and moving AWAY: 떠나다 = leave/depart. Compare 도착하다, arrive.
기차 = train; 역 = 驛, station. Picture a TRAIN stopping under a giant station sign: 기차역. 역 also appears in 지하철역, subway station.
교 = 敎, teaching; 회 = 會, gathering. A gathering for religious teaching → CHURCH. Link 회 with 회의실, a room for a meeting/gathering.
회의 = meeting; 실 = 室, room. MEETING ROOM. Imagine colleagues arguing around a table; same 실 as 미용실, a beauty room/salon.
sa-jeon → 'SAGE JOHN knows every WORD'. Picture wise John sitting inside a DICTIONARY, explaining every word you point at. Sound trick, not an origin.
시 = 時, time; 계 = 計, measure. TIME MEASURER → clock/watch. Imagine a clock measuring the seconds until your exam.
달 = month; 력 = 曆, calendar. A calendar shows the MONTHS. Picture flipping one 달 every time you turn a calendar page.
mu-geop → 'MOVE? GULP!' A suitcase is so HEAVY you gulp before lifting it. Opposite 가볍다, light.

note: 무겁습니다 is the formal polite form of 무겁다. Opposite: 가볍다, light.

memoryHint.text: Picture a DAILY round trip to school/work: 다니다 = go regularly / attend / commute. 다닙니다 is its polite form, not a different word.

note: 다닙니다 is the formal polite form of 다니다. 학교에 다니다 = attend school; 회사에 다니다 = work at / commute to a company. It suggests regular or repeated going.

meanings: who is / who stays (honorific modifier) / находящийся (уваж.)

occurrences.meaning: who is / who stays (honorific modifier) / находящийся (уваж.)

memoryHint.text: 계시다 respectfully replaces 있다 when a PERSON is somewhere. 선생님이 계신 곳 = the place where the teacher is. 계신 is the describing form.

answer: who is / who stays (honorific modifier) / находящийся (уваж.)
note: 계신 is the noun-modifying form of 계시다: 선생님이 계신 곳 = where the teacher is. Use 계시다 for respectfully referring to a person, not an ordinary object.

memoryHint.text: 화 = 畫, painting; 가 = 家, specialist here. A PAINTING specialist → painter. In 화가 나다, however, 화 is anger and 가 is a particle.

note: 화가 (畫家) by itself = painter. In 화가 나다, 화 means anger and 가 is a subject particle: 화가 나요 = I am angry / get angry. These are different uses.

memoryHint.text: 장미 = rose; 꽃 = flower. ROSE FLOWER. Picture a huge rose blooming from the tiny word 꽃.

note: 장미 = rose; 꽃 = flower. Both 장미 and 장미꽃 can refer to a rose.

meanings: have done something before / когда-либо делать раньше

occurrences.meaning: have done something before / когда-либо делать раньше

memoryHint.text: 적 = occasion/experience; 있다 = exists. An experience EXISTS → have done it before. 간 적이 있어요 = I have been there before.

answer: have done something before / когда-либо делать раньше
quizAnswer: have done something before / иметь опыт чего-либо
note: Use -ㄴ after a vowel and -은 after a consonant: 간 적이 있다 = have gone before; 먹은 적이 있다 = have eaten before. Negative: -(으)ㄴ 적이 없다, have never done it.

memoryHint.text: 일기 = diary (daily record); 장 = 帳, notebook/register. A DIARY NOTEBOOK full of your daily thoughts.

meanings: move to another place / spread; be transmitted / перемещаться; передаваться

occurrences.meaning: move to another place / spread; be transmitted / перемещаться; передаваться

memoryHint.text: Picture a rumour or cold JUMPING from one person to another: it SPREADS. 옮다 also describes moving between places; 옮기다 moves something else.

answer: move to another place / spread; be transmitted / перемещаться; передаваться
quizAnswer: move / spread / be transmitted / перемещаться; передаваться
note: A real verb, pronounced 옴따. It can mean move between places or spread/be transmitted (감기가 옮다). 옮기다 means move/transfer something or pass something on. 옳다 is a different word meaning correct/right.

memoryHint.text: 자기 = oneself; 를 = object marker; 지키다 = protect; -는 describes a noun. 자기를 지키는 방법 = a method for PROTECTING ONESELF.

note: 자기 = oneself; 지키다 = protect; -는 makes a noun modifier. 자기를 지키는 방법 = a method of protecting oneself. It is not a full sentence by itself.

memoryHint.text: 늘다 = INCREASE / IMPROVE, but 늘 = always. Picture your Korean ability growing UP: 한국어가 늘어요. Opposite 줄다, decrease (not 줄이다, reduce something).

note: 한국어가 늘었어요 = my Korean improved. 늘다 is different from 늘 (always) and 늘리다 (increase something). Its intransitive opposite is 줄다 (decrease); 줄이다 means reduce something.
